title: Universal Logic Engine Specification Review
source: User-provided critique in MKC ARCHIVE conversation
classification: user-supplied proposals and technical claims; not independently verified
summary: Ten proposed refinements to a Universal Logic Engine architecture, with USC identified as the highest-priority proposal.

proposals.name: Universal State Chain (USC)
proposals.caveat: Hash chain does not prove evidence truth; canonicalization, trust anchors, and key management required.

proposals.name: Expanded transition evidence record
proposals.caveat: Signature field is underspecified; total assumes fixed-width fields without framing or metadata.

proposals.name: Speculative Continuation Mode
proposals.mechanism: Execute provisional predicted state while a missing tile loads, then reconcile through verifier
proposals.caveat: Requires provisional semantics, rollback, dependency tracking, and side-effect isolation.

proposals.name: Bounded canonical folding
proposals.caveat: Finite tests alone do not justify universal error probability; distribution and test design required.

proposals.name: Transfer-aware learning/forgetting
proposals.caveat: T and F not operationally defined or normalized.

proposals.name: Adversarial truth test
proposals.caveat: Retrieval coverage, scoring, and thresholds undefined; cannot guarantee truth.

proposals.name: Minimum retained entropy
proposals.trigger: if H < H_min then decompress or restore attractor
proposals.caveat: Entropy proxy, units, measurement window, and safeguards undefined.

proposals.name: Statistical policy promotion
proposals.criterion: utility gain AND safety holds AND p < 0.01
proposals.caveat: Requires endpoint, power, effect size, multiple-testing and sequential-testing protocol.

proposals.name: Epistemic mortality
proposals.caveat: Requires evidence weighting, dependency handling, time decay, and reversible archive semantics.

established_from_source: User requested knowledge harvesting of this critique.
The critique identifies USC as its highest-priority proposed addition.
open_questions: Identify authoritative baseline specification and version.
Choose hash/signature/MAC scheme, key lifecycle, and trusted checkpoints.
Specify speculative state rollback and reconciliation.
Define statistical model for canonical-fold error target.
Define statistical promotion protocol and safety criteria.
Confirm whether MIE, EVOLUTION-X, CGIOF, WPA, NOESIS, USC labels are established project terms.
verification_notes: Hash-chain integrity is not equivalent to truth.
A finite corpus does not by itself prove a universal probabilistic error bound.
p < 0.01 alone does not establish practical value or safety.
All proposals require explicit adoption, specification, and testing before being described as implemented.
